# DeepSage

> DeepSage publishes free AI-generated articles and interactive quizzes, and is building educational games and story-driven books (in development) about real-world skills -- AI literacy, data analysis, critical thinking, foreign languages and more.

## Key pages
- [Home](https://deepsage.com/): what DeepSage is and how it works
- [Articles](https://deepsage.com/article/): full article index
- [Quizzes](https://deepsage.com/quiz/): full quiz index
- [Skills](https://deepsage.com/skills/): 40 skill guides, including 10 foreign languages
- [Games](https://deepsage.com/games/): upcoming skill-building games (in development)
- [Books](https://deepsage.com/books/): one story-driven book per skill (in development)

## Recent articles
- [The cosmic static you weren't supposed to hear](https://deepsage.com/article/the-cosmic-static-you-weren-t-supposed-to-hear/): How a persistent radio hum and a group of guys looking for a ghost turned a hardware nuisance into the birth certificate of the universe.
- [The 2,000-Year-Old Bronze Lump That Might Be the World's First Computer](https://deepsage.com/article/the-2-000-year-old-bronze-lump-that-might-be-the-world-s-first-computer/): Forget silicon chips; the ancient Greeks were doing high-level math with nothing but bronze, teeth, and some seriously impressive gear ratios.
- [The Great Data Rot of Alexandria](https://deepsage.com/article/the-great-data-rot-of-alexandria/): The Library of Alexandria didn't die in a blaze of glory; it died because someone forgot to pay the subscription fee for the ink.
- [The universe is just a very loud error message](https://deepsage.com/article/the-universe-is-just-a-very-loud-error-message/): The discovery of the Cosmic Microwave Background wasn't a victory lap for physics; it was a desperate attempt to clean some pigeon droppings off a radio antenna.
- [The Moldy Saddle and the Laboratory Machine](https://deepsage.com/article/the-moldy-saddle-and-the-laboratory-machine/): Alexander Fleming didn't invent penicillin; he just happened to be the person who built a very expensive way to formalize what stablemen had been doing for years.
- [The Ancient Greek User Interface](https://deepsage.com/article/the-ancient-greek-user-interface/): It wasn't just a calculator for the stars; it was a way to make the universe's math visible to the masses.
- [The Antikythera Mechanism: A Hardware Interface for a Lost Library](https://deepsage.com/article/the-antikythera-mechanism-a-hardware-interface-for-a-lost-library/): It wasn't just a calculator; it was a portable display for a missing collection of ancient Greek code.
- [The Bronze Machine that Refused to Accept Wrong Answers](https://deepsage.com/article/the-bronze-machine-that-refused-to-accept-wrong-answers/): The Antikythera Mechanism wasn't just a calendar; it was a mechanical attempt to force the universe to behave.
- [The $3,000 Chocolate Bar That Changed Dinner Forever](https://deepsage.com/article/the-3-000-chocolate-bar-that-changed-dinner-forever/): How a melted snack in a radar engineer's pocket led to the most essential kitchen appliance in history.
- [320°C, No Sunlight, and a Very Spicy Soup](https://deepsage.com/article/320-c-no-sunlight-and-a-very-spicy-soup/): Deep-sea hydrothermal vents are basically the Earth's way of running a high-pressure, chemically volatile experiment that life actually enjoys.
- [The Bronze Driver for a Lost Universe](https://deepsage.com/article/the-bronze-driver-for-a-lost-universe/): What if the world's first computer wasn't the main event, but just the peripheral for a much larger, missing system?
- [The Victorian Flower Hack: Why You Should Never Send a Basil Bouquet](https://deepsage.com/article/the-victorian-flower-hack-why-you-should-never-send-a-basil-bouquet/): Before emojis, there were hydrangeas, and they were much harder to misinterpret without accidentally declaring war.
- [The Discovery of Cosmic Microwave Background Radiation via the Holmdel Antenna](https://deepsage.com/article/the-discovery-of-cosmic-microwave-background-radiation-via-the-holmdel-antenna/): An analysis of how Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson identified a persistent 3 Kelvin signal that provided empirical evidence for the Big Bang model.
- [The Bronze Compiler: Decoding Ancient Greece's Lost Hardware](https://deepsage.com/article/the-bronze-compiler-decoding-ancient-greece-s-lost-hardware/): The Antikythera Mechanism wasn't just a clock; it was the physical execution of a lost programming language written in bronze.
- [The Bronze Orphan: Why the Antikythera Mechanism shouldn't exist](https://deepsage.com/article/the-bronze-orphan-why-the-antikythera-mechanism-shouldn-t-exist/): It was a hand-cranked computer from 150 BCE that predicted eclipses with terrifying precision, but the tools to build it seem to have vanished from history.
- [The 2,000-Year-Old Glitch in Our History Books](https://deepsage.com/article/the-2-000-year-old-glitch-in-our-history-books/): A corroded bronze lump from a Roman shipwreck is making historians rethink everything they thought they knew about ancient technology.
- [The Emu War: Why the Australian Army Lost to a Bird (and the Political Plot You Missed)](https://deepsage.com/article/the-emu-war-why-the-australian-army-lost-to-a-bird-and-the-political-plot-you-missed/): It wasn't just about protecting wheat; it was a high-stakes psychological operation to keep a country from falling apart.
- [Taming Chance. Part 1: How Often Does Chance Alone Build Streaks? Cicero's Dice Answer](https://deepsage.com/article/how-often-does-chance-alone-build-streaks-ciceros-dice-answer/): Why a 22-game winning streak, a 17-round losing run or a cluster of coincidences can be ordinary, how often chance builds them, and one question that sorts luck from cause.
- [The Salty Mystery of the Archaean Oceans](https://deepsage.com/article/the-salty-mystery-of-the-archaean-oceans/): Before the first microbes even learned to breathe, Earth's oceans might have been a much more intense brine than the seas we swim in today.
- [The Screwdriver That Triggered a Nuclear Nightmare](https://deepsage.com/article/the-screwdriver-that-triggered-a-nuclear-nightmare/): A single slip of a tool turned a softball-sized sphere of plutonium into a lethal radiation engine.
- [The R101: Britain's Great Airship Disaster](https://deepsage.com/article/the-r101-britain-s-billion-dollar-sky-disaster/): Before we had drones to spy on neighbors, Britain tried to conquer the clouds with a giant, flammable, and incredibly expensive balloon.
- [The 3-Solar-Mass Magic Trick](https://deepsage.com/article/the-3-solar-mass-magic-trick/): When two black holes collided, they vanished a whole chunk of mass into pure energy: ripples in spacetime that our instruments could measure.
- [The Italian Diaspora and the Ghost of 'La Dolce Vita'](https://deepsage.com/article/the-italian-diaspora-and-the-ghost-of-la-dolce-vita/): Behind every great pasta sauce in a suburban kitchen lies a profound, unshakeable longing for a home that might not even exist anymore.
- [The Great Cosmic Expansion: Stretching or Just Adding More Stuff?](https://deepsage.com/article/the-great-cosmic-expansion-stretching-or-just-adding-more-stuff/): Whether space is stretching like old spandex or spawning new pixels, the math says we're getting bigger.
- [The 'Hard Choice' Trap: Why Logic Fails When Life Gets Real](https://deepsage.com/article/the-hard-choice-trap-why-logic-fails-when-life-gets-real/): If you're paralyzed by a decision where both options look equally good (or equally terrible), you aren't bad at math—you're just facing a structural philosophical crisis.
- [Why Your 'Natural Talent' is Probably a Lie](https://deepsage.com/article/why-your-natural-talent-is-probably-a-lie/): Forget everything you thought you knew about being a prodigy; it turns out greatness is less about DNA and more about the room you're standing in.
- [The Universe is Expanding, and It's Not Taking Us With It](https://deepsage.com/article/the-universe-is-expanding-and-it-s-not-taking-us-with-it/): A century ago, we didn't even know the universe was growing; now we know it's planning a very lonely exit strategy.
- [The Petrified Forest Conscience Files](https://deepsage.com/article/the-petrified-forest-conscience-files/): Why people are mailing rocks back to a National Park in a bizarre ritual of geological guilt.
- [Constantin Brancusi: The Man Who Taught Modernity How to Smooth Out Its Edges](https://deepsage.com/article/constantin-brancusi-the-man-who-taught-modernity-how-to-smooth-out-its-edges/): Long before Silicon Valley obsessed over 'seamless user experiences,' one Romanian sculptor was already perfecting the art of the minimalist curve.
- [The Physical Internet: Why We Stopped Sending Cats Through Pipes](https://deepsage.com/article/the-physical-internet-why-we-stopped-sending-cats-through-pipes/): Before we had packets of data, we had packets of everything, including, famously, a live cat.
